title: On the integration of lightweight tasks with MPI using the C++26 std::execution 'Senders' API
problem: Integrating asynchronous MPI messaging with tasking runtimes requires careful handling of request polling and completion dispatching. Existing approaches lack clean abstractions for this integration.
motivation: Hybrid programming (MPI + tasks) is important for HPC but requires careful synchronization. C++26 Senders API provides new abstractions for expressing asynchronous execution and data flow, enabling cleaner MPI-task integration.
method: Implement Senders API in pika tasking runtime. Wrap asynchronous MPI calls as execution nodes in computation graph. Experiment with different polling and completion dispatching strategies.
key_novelty: First implementation of C++26 Senders API in HPC tasking runtime (pika); MPI as first-class nodes in execution graph; explicit scheduling and execution placement.
contributions: Implementation of major C++26 Senders API features in pika
Integration of asynchronous MPI with tasking through Senders
Insights on polling and completion task scheduling strategies
Analysis of performance impact from scheduling choices
hardware_target: Generic HPC systems with MPI support

metrics.performance: Application performance affected by scheduling/placement choices

limitations: Abstract only; no performance benchmarks; scheduling strategy comparison not detailed; scalability evaluation unclear.
